newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Centam nations to split ACPC extra coffee quotas.
newsitem.headline: Centam nations to split ACPC extra coffee quotas.

text.p: El Salvador and Costa Rica will split an additional allotment of coffee exports in the first half of 1997 that has been earmarked by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), Salvadoran coffee leaders said Thursday.

Ruben Pineda and Herbert de Sola told Reuters that the extra 200,000 60-kg bags of exports that the ACPC decided at a recent London meeting to release will be divided 50-50 between the two Central American nations.

"In principle, it will be split 100,000 bags for each country," Pineda said. "It could be a little more or a little less for either country, that just depends how the (1996-1997) crops end for the two countries," the executive director of the Salvadoran Coffee Council said.

The ACPC decided March 20 in London to release an extra 200,000 bags of arabicas to world markets under the cartel's export quota scheme that is designed to control bean flows and maintain coffee prices.

"There were only two arabica producing nations that wanted extra quotas and they were Costa Rica and El Salvador," De Sola also told Reuters. "That's where the quotas are going to be shared," he added.

"The two coffee bodies of the two countries are still revising figures, it is a gradual process with both countries in consultation with each other, as I have said it is just fine tuning and not really much coffee," the Central American representative to the ACPC said.
Market talk had wondered if Colombia and Honduras could also bid for part of the additional 200,000 bag quota. Both Salvadoran coffee leaders denied the versions.
